A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TFM-Tokenizer research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original EEG classification, ear-EEG sleep staging, token-quality, transfer, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, ear-EEG integration results, parameter ablations, and training-loss curves.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 retain the dual-path encoder, vector quantization, masking objectives, and downstream training procedure. Appendix E elaborates integrations already described in v2 Section 4.3. Renaming frequency-bin masking to frequency-band masking does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TUEV, TUAB, IIIC Seizure, CHB-MIT, and EESM23 ear-EEG sleep staging. Cross-dataset transfer already appears in v2 Appendix C.3. The additions use retained datasets and tasks without introducing a distinct population or test environment.

E2.justification: v4 adds CBraMod to the multiple-dataset comparisons on all four main benchmarks in Tables 1–2. Table 3 adds BIOT-TFM and LaBraM-TFM to the ear-EEG comparison; these integrations previously appeared only in other comparisons. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: New ablations vary frequency masking ratios, window/hop combinations with aligned STFT settings, and embedding dimensions from 32 to 256. The masking-ratio experiment fixes temporal masking at 0.5 and disables symmetric masking. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, training budgets, and default window and embedding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.10–C.12 substantially extend sensitivity analysis to masking strength across three datasets, temporal segmentation, and embedding width. Figure 12 adds training-behavior analysis for both pretraining stages. These address additional questions about design robustness; Figure 8 merely redraws the retained masked-token-prediction ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Appendix B.4. v4 removes the p = 1.5e-4 significance report for the IIIC comparison with LaBraM in Section 4.2, while retaining the ear-EEG p = 0.02. No increase in runs or new statistical procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are retained, but CBraMod, ear-EEG integration, sensitivity, and training-curve results substantially extend the empirical findings. CBraMod takes the multiple-dataset CHB-MIT AUROC lead at 0.9071 versus TFM-Tokenizer's unchanged 0.8818. New window/hop results span TUEV kappa values of 0.0168–0.6059 in Table 14, revealing substantial setting dependence rather than a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, STFT formulation, quantization rule, and training objectives in Section 3 and Appendix A are unchanged. The added motif explanation and empirical interpretations introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction reduce the highlighted relative performance advantage from 17% to approximately 11%, reflecting the stronger CBraMod comparison rather than changed TFM-Tokenizer scores. The central contributions concerning single-channel motif tokenization, model integration, and cross-device scalability remain.

C2.justification: New discussions explain masking-ratio selection, associate shorter windows with finer motifs, hypothesize instability with larger embeddings, and interpret loss curves as evidence of stable training. The existing fixed-window limitation remains. Appendix C.10 incorrectly calls the CHB-MIT exception Cohen's Kappa, although Table 13 reports AUC-PR.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds implementation details for BIOT embeddings and training stages, and explicitly explains LaBraM-TFM target generation and tokenizer removal before fine-tuning. Appendix C.10 discloses the selected frequency masking ratio. Existing hyperparameter tables and code/model-access statements are retained; these additions do not establish changes to the earlier implementations.

R1.justification: v4 adds the CBraMod reference, Wang et al. (2024d), and incorporates it into comparative positioning in Section 4.2 and Tables 1–2. Section 2 and the frequency-representation-collapse discussion, moved from Appendix E to F, otherwise retain their substantive positioning.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify motifs and explicit frequency modeling, standardize masking and downstream-model terminology, and update author contact information and the publication header. Additional appendix subsections and the integration appendix expand the structure, but the main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v4 expands Tables 1–3, adds ablation Tables 13–15 and Figures 12–13, and redraws Figure 8 as a combined display of the same results. Appendix pagination and float placement change, while the original visual format and most existing figures and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: v4 provides useful additional evidence about parameter sensitivity, incorporates a stronger comparator with a correspondingly narrower headline advantage, and clarifies existing model integrations. These incrementally strengthen an already extensively evaluated paper. The new CHB-MIT metric mislabel and removal of one significance report are limited reporting weaknesses that temper, but do not outweigh, these gains.
